London Advanced · Journal

London, reported
from the pavement.

Places, walks and details that reward a second look. Written from direct experience, checked against sources and paired with original photography.

By Paolo Pastorino
Latest stories

No artificial publishing quota: only work that earns the reader’s time.

South-east London · Walking route

Blackheath to Greenwich: the slow way down the hill

Start with village shops, cross the open heath and enter Greenwich Park from above. The famous view comes later; the quieter route towards it is the real pleasure.

27 September 2026Read →
City of London · Urban walks

The City of London dragon walk: follow the boundary most people miss

White dragons stand guard where the City begins. Link them together and a familiar business district turns into a walk through boundaries, lost gates and stubborn fragments of old London.

27 September 2026Read →
City of London · Free viewpoints

One Leadenhall terrace: London’s best new low-level view?

This is not another race to the top of the skyline. Four floors above Leadenhall Market, the terrace succeeds because the City remains close enough to read.

27 September 2026Read →
Clerkenwell · Illustration

Quentin Blake Centre for Illustration: beyond the familiar drawings

London’s new home for illustration uses a beautifully restored industrial site to make the case that drawings are not the supporting act. They are the story.

27 September 2026Read →
Leamouth · Industrial London

Trinity Buoy Wharf: London’s lighthouse at the edge of the Thames

A lighthouse that never guided ships to sea, a composition designed to last a thousand years and one of east London’s strangest riverside corners.

27 September 2026Read →
Hackney Wick · Museums

V&A East Storehouse: the museum that shows its workings

Half a million objects, open storage and a museum that turns its backstage machinery into part of the visit. The scale is striking; the freedom to follow your own curiosity is the real point.

27 September 2026Read →
